name: glb-designer-simple
description: IXT-SUITES simple rung for the GLB asset designer (`ui/glbEditor/GlbDesignerDialog.tsx`, catalog footer 'Design' button / ⌘K, pro-only — gated directly on `uiMode === 'pro'`, not a FEATURE_FLAGS entry). Confirms the dialog stays unmounted in Simple mode even when `glbDesignerOpen` is forced true, then in Pro mode drives a REAL edit (not just 'dialog opened'): add a box, change its size + position through the controlled numeric inputs, name it, Save, and assert the save round-trips into the actual Zustand store (`state.userFurniture` gains a `UserGltfDef` with the given name/category, length increments past a recorded baseline) — the same commit path a real upload uses (`persistUserGlb` -> `addUserFurniture`). Gated on the store round-trip (not the auto-dismissing success toast), which is the definitive proof. NOTE the Save click uses a DOM `.click()` eval, not the harness text-click, because the 'Save to catalog' button is below the fold in the scrolling right panel and the coordinate-based text-click would miss it — see the scenario's click-save comment + the playbook gotcha. Finishes by switching back to Simple and re-confirming the dialog stays hidden. The dialog is `React.lazy` (`ui/app/lazyComponents.tsx`) but is also in `preloadOnIdle.ts`'s `PRELOAD_ORDER`, so by the time this scenario's `waitFor: {text: '3D asset designer'}` step runs (after several earlier steps' worth of idle time), the chunk is already resident and Suspense resolves immediately — see the playbook's 'Lazy panels mount seconds after their store flag flips' gotcha; no dev-only mounting lever was needed. The complementary complex rung (`glb-csg-textures-simple.json`) covers per-part finishes + CSG boolean combine + reopen-resets; this rung intentionally stays to the tier-gate + minimal edit + store round-trip so the two don't duplicate coverage.

steps.name: click-save
steps.comment: Click 'Save asset' via a DOM .click(), NOT the harness text-click. The button lives in the 'Save to catalog' section at the very BOTTOM of the scrolling right panel (overflowY:auto) — below the fold at every viewport. clickByText (scripts/lib/interact.mjs) clicks the element's bounding-rect centre with page.mouse.click WITHOUT scrolling it into view, so a below-the-fold button is silently missed and save() never fires (this is exactly why the existing glb-csg-textures-simple.json save step also times out). A programmatic .click() dispatches a real click event that React's onClick honours regardless of scroll position. The export/persist path itself is fully headless-drivable (GLTFExporter import + parse verified working; persistUserGlb is exercised headless by the bulk-import scenarios).
steps.eval: (function(){ const btn = [...document.querySelectorAll('button')].find(b => b.textContent.trim() === 'Save asset' && !b.disabled); if (!btn) throw new Error('Save asset button not found or disabled'); btn.scrollIntoView(); btn.click(); })()

steps.name: assert-userfurniture-roundtrip
steps.comment: The REAL round-trip proof: the save path (buildEditedObject -> exportGlb -> persistUserGlb -> addUserFurniture) must add a UserGltfDef with our name/category to the actual Zustand store. Generous timeout — GLTFExporter serialisation + IDB write take a moment in SwiftShader headless.

waitFor.store: state.userFurniture.length > window.__glbBaseline && state.userFurniture.some(d => d.name === 'IXT Simple Box' && d.category === 'others' && d.source === 'user')
